title: Idempotent replay coordinator with time-window sharding for analytics backfills
creator: Marco Chen
description: Build a resilient, idempotent replay coordinator service that can orchestrate backfills and targeted replays for console usage analytics. The coordinator should partition work into time-window shards, provide durable checkpoints, and produce deterministic, replayable batches for downstream consumers (batch enrichment, aggregation, and time-series exporters). This ticket covers the coordinator service, shard assignment logic, checkpoint schema, and operational tooling to run large-scale reprocesses without corrupting existing aggregates.
background: We currently run ad-hoc reprocess jobs that are brittle at scale: retries create duplicate events in downstream OLAP tables, and long-running jobs lose progress on instance restarts. Recent customer-facing regressions (see CON-2389) highlight the need for a repeatable, observable replay mechanism for console metrics, token billing events, and route-level latency traces. The solution should support both full backfills and selective replays (by project, route, or model), with clear stop/resume semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can schedule and run a replay across a 30-day window by sharding time into configurable windows (default 1h) and redistributing work across workers
Each shard has a durable checkpoint stored in our metadata store (Postgres) and can be retried without double-writing downstream targets
Downstream consumers receive monotonic sequence IDs per-event and consumer-side dedup prevents duplicates when replaying the same shard
Operational runbooks exist: start/stop/retry, progress dashboard, and cost estimates for 1M events
End-to-end test harness with synthetic events demonstrates idempotent behavior and <0.5% false-positive dedup rate
tasks: Design shard key and time-window scheme (1h/15m configurable)
Implement coordinator API (start, pause, resume, cancel, status)
Checkpointing layer in Postgres with optimistic concurrency and lease TTL
Worker library for deterministic batch generation and enriched event formatting
Consumer dedup protocol (monotonic seq + event fingerprint) and SDK changes
Integrate with existing reprocess orchestration UI in Console
Add progress & cost telemetry to Grafana dashboard
Write e2e test suite and run a small-scale backfill for verification
design_decisions: Use time-window shards (configurable) instead of source-partition sharding to simplify cutoff semantics across heterogeneous sources
Store checkpoints in Postgres to leverage existing backups/audit trails rather than introducing a new state store
Favor at-least-once production with idempotent writes and consumer-side dedup instead of attempting distributed exactly-once to reduce runtime complexity
Lease TTL + optimistic update chosen to handle worker restarts without a heavy heartbeat protocol
tradeoffs: Postgres checkpointing is easier to operate but may add contention for very high shard counts; mitigation: shard coalescing and read replicas for status queries
Consumer-side dedup requires schema changes (monotonic seq + fingerprint) and small storage overhead but avoids coupling coordinator to every downstream system
Longer shard windows reduce metadata overhead but increase runtime per worker and failure blast radius
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete — prototype coordinator that slices a 24h range into 1h shards and persists checkpoints in a local dev Postgres (branch: feat/rep-coordinator-spike)

2026-02-18: Design review with Eng + PM + Design. Agreed on Postgres checkpoint schema and lease model. Action: add TTL and exponential backoff for stuck shards (notes: /docs/confluence/rep-coordinator/design-2026-02-18)
2026-02-24: Initial API landed (PR: github.com/redwood/console-backend/pull/4567) — start/pause/resume endpoints present, basic auth and audit fields added
2026-02-27: Worker library published as internal package registry @redwood/rep-worker v0.1.0. Integration tests show deterministic batch ordering for synthetic event set
2026-03-01: End-to-end smoke run against staging completed for a 6h window across 4 workers. Observed duplicates due to consumer SDK race; created follow-up ENG-18221 to fix consumer dedup SDK
review_feedback: Elena Vasquez (SRE): add circuit breaker to prevent runaway replays from exhausting DB connections
Rohan Mehta (PM): ensure cost telemetry emitted per-shard to estimate total reprocess spend upfront
Team Lead (Anika Singh): prefer eventual consistency on shard status queries and avoid synchronous blocking calls from Console UI
open_risks: High-volume replays could saturate downstream OLAP imports and invalidate incremental aggregates — mitigation: throttling policy and pre-check dry-run
Schema migrations for monotonic seq may require backfill in BigQuery; need migration plan and a compatibility mode
Operator error when cancelling mid-run could leave partial aggregates; runbook must include reconcile steps
next_steps: Finish consumer dedup SDK fixes (ENG-18221) and coordinate a staged release
Add shard-level throttling and cost estimation to coordinator API
Run a controlled 7-day backfill on staging and validate aggregates against golden dataset
Create Console UI integration ticket to expose run controls and progress bars
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint TTL and lease takeover semantics
Integration test: synthetic 100k events replay with two restarts mid-run to validate idempotency
Performance test: run 1M-event backfill in staging and measure DB load and downstream latency
Chaos test: kill worker process during shard execution and verify lease takeover within TTL
